goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/embed/best.html.erb:2 — `@topic_view.posts` dereferenced unconditionally while the spec's stubbed TopicView returns nil, raising NoMethodError (P1)

adjudication.rationale: `app/views/embed/best.html.erb` dereferences `@topic_view.posts`, but `EmbedController#best` only renders the `best` template when `topic_id` is present and it assigns `@topic_view = TopicView.new(...)` in that branch. When `topic_id` is nil it renders `loading` instead, so `best.html.erb` is not evaluated without `@topic_view`. The spec’s `TopicView.expects(:new).with(...)` not specifying a return value would only matter if the view were rendered in the controller spec (typically it is not unless `render_views` is enabled), and it does not indicate a production bug in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:44 — `open(url).read` relies on open-uri which is required only in poll_feed.rb, so TopicRetriever/disqus paths can raise Errno::ENOENT (P2)

adjudication.rationale: Yes. `TopicEmbed.import_remote` calls `open(url).read` but does not `require 'open-uri'` (and neither `topic_embed.rb` nor `topic_retriever.rb` nor `disqus.thor` requires it). In Ruby, without open-uri loaded, `Kernel#open` will treat an `http(s)://...` string as a local path, which can raise `Errno::ENOENT` instead of performing an HTTP fetch. The diff explicitly adds `require 'open-uri'` only in `poll_feed.rb`, so the TopicRetriever/disqus code paths can fail at runtime unless some other unrelated file happens to load open-uri.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:117 — --category option deleted and import_remote now does a live HTTP fetch per thread, dropping created_at and skipping threads with dead links (P2)

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the Disqus Thor task's `--category` option and the logic that looked up `category_id`, so imports can no longer target a category (feature regression). It also replaces `PostCreator.new(... created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]) ...)` with `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, which performs a live `open(url).read` HTTP fetch in `TopicEmbed.import_remote` and does not pass/preserve `created_at`. There is no rescue around the network fetch, so dead/unreachable links would raise and can break the import run (at minimum, behavior is now dependent on external HTTP availability).

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:1 — no spec renders best.html.erb or loading.html.erb, so the entire rendered-output half of the feature is unverified (P0)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds controller specs for `EmbedController#best`, but they only assert response success/headers and mocking behavior; they do not enable `render_views` or assert on the rendered body, so the ERB templates aren’t exercised by these tests. However, this is a test-coverage critique rather than a concrete bug/security/correctness defect in the implementation introduced by the diff. The code can still function correctly without view-rendering tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/post.rb:133 — `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` stores third-party HTML as cooked with no sanitization and no spec asserts stripping (P1)

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new `cook_method` enum and changes `Post#cook` to `return raw` when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, explicitly bypassing the normal cooking/rendering pipeline (which is where Discourse typically sanitizes/filters HTML). The new `TopicEmbed.import` and `PollFeed` paths feed third-party HTML (`SimpleRSS` item content after `CGI.unescapeHTML`, and `Readability::Document#content` from remote pages) into `PostCreator` with `cook_method: :raw_html`, meaning that third-party HTML will be stored/served as `cooked` without sanitization. The added spec (`topic_embed_spec`) even asserts `post.cooked == post.raw`, reinforcing that no stripping/sanitization is expected. This is a real, verifiable security/correctness issue (potential XSS) introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:34-37 — update branch calls PostRevisor.new(embed.post) with no nil guard; a deleted post aborts the whole hourly feed import (P1)

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the update path does `post = embed.post` and then unconditionally does `revisor = PostRevisor.new(post)` if the SHA changed. Because the `topic_embeds.post_id` association is not protected by a foreign key in this diff, `embed.post` can be `nil` (e.g., if the referenced Post row was deleted), and `PostRevisor` will then raise when it tries to use `@post` (e.g., `@post.acting_user = ...` in `revise!`). That exception would bubble up and abort the importing job (e.g., `Jobs::PollFeed`), so the lack of a nil guard is a real correctness risk in the added code path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:56-70 — absolutize_urls only rewrites paths starting with '/', corrupting protocol-relative //cdn URLs and leaving plain relative paths broken (P2)

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls, links/images are rewritten only when href/src starts_with?('/') (lines ~56-70). This will also match protocol-relative URLs like "//cdn.example.com/x" and incorrectly rewrite them to the source host (e.g., "http://sourcehost/cdn.example.com/x") because it strips all leading slashes via sub(/^\/+/, ''). Additionally, non-root-relative paths like "images/foo.png" are not rewritten at all despite the method’s stated purpose to make relative URLs absolute, leaving them potentially broken in the imported HTML.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 — `contents << "\n<hr>..."` mutates the caller's string, double-appending the footer or raising on a frozen literal (P2)

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.import`, line `contents << "\n<hr>..."` uses `String#<<`, which mutates the `contents` object provided by the caller. This is directly verifiable from the diff. Because the method doesn’t `dup`/copy the string first, any caller that reuses the same string instance (e.g., calling `import` twice with the same `contents` variable/object) would end up with the footer appended multiple times, and if `contents` is ever a frozen string, this will raise `FrozenError`/`RuntimeError` depending on Ruby version.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26 — exact-string host match rejects www./uppercase/multi-host embeddable hosts with no acceptance criterion or spec (P2)

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, the code deliberately enforces a single allowed embedding host by checking `URI(request.referer || '').host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host` and raising on mismatch. The site setting is explicitly singular (“Host that can embed…”), so an exact host match is consistent with the intended configuration model. Rejecting `www.` vs non-`www.` is a predictable outcome that can be handled by setting `embeddable_host` to the exact desired host; multi-host support is not implied by the diff. Also, Ruby’s `URI#host` is normalized (lowercased), so “uppercase” rejection is not clearly a real issue. The “no acceptance criterion/spec” part is not a verifiable defect in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb:1 — no spec file for Jobs::RetrieveTopic anywhere, so arg validation and staff no_throttle bypass are unverified (P2)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new job `app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb` but does not add a corresponding spec file for it. While that’s true, “no spec exists so behavior is unverified” is a test-coverage concern rather than a verifiable bug/security/correctness defect introduced by the diff. The job’s argument validation and `no_throttle` behavior are implemented directly in the code and there’s no concrete malfunction shown in the diff that would make this a real problem by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:11 — unique index on embed_url with no validates_uniqueness_of, so the acknowledged race surfaces as raw RecordNotUnique (P2)

adjudication.rationale: The migration adds a UNIQUE index on topic_embeds.embed_url, but the TopicEmbed model only validates presence (no uniqueness). In TopicEmbed.import it does a read-then-create pattern: `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and if blank proceeds to `TopicEmbed.create!`. Under concurrent imports of the same URL (e.g., multiple retrieve jobs/requests), both can observe no row and then attempt `create!`, causing the DB unique index to raise an unhandled `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` exception. While uniqueness validation wouldn’t fully eliminate races, the diff does introduce an unhandled uniqueness-violation failure mode tied to the unique index and lack of application-level handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:4 — edit to an already-shipped unrelated migration adding `force: true`, untraceable to embed URL handling (P1)

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes an existing migration (CreateTopTopics) to use `create_table :top_topics, force: true`. This is an unrelated change, but it is not a clear, verifiable defect introduced by the diff: migrations are not re-run on already-migrated production databases, so it won’t affect existing installs. For fresh installs, `force: true` behaves the same as normal `create_table` when the table doesn’t already exist. The finding mainly objects to modifying an old migration and being unrelated to embedding, which is a process/style concern rather than a concrete bug/security/correctness problem evidenced in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:117 — the --category CLI option and category_id lookup are silently deleted, a user-facing functional regression outside stated scope (P1)

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the Disqus Thor task's `--category/-c` option (`method_option :category`) and deletes the associated `category_id` lookup and passing `category: category_id` into `PostCreator`. The new code path uses `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, and `TopicEmbed.import_remote` / `TopicEmbed.import` do not accept or apply a category. This is a verifiable behavior change: the CLI can no longer import Disqus threads into a specified category, which is a user-facing functional regression introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: docs/tasks/task-001.md:1 — the diff introduces the entire embedding feature (controller, jobs, views, RSS polling, cook_method) rather than enhancing existing URL handling/validation (P1)

adjudication.rationale: The proposed finding is about scope/intent (“introduces the entire embedding feature rather than enhancing existing URL handling/validation”) rather than identifying a concrete defect (bug/security/correctness) introduced by the diff. The diff clearly adds new embedding/RSS/import functionality intentionally (new controller, jobs, models, routes, settings, assets). Nothing in the finding points to a verifiable problem in the code itself—it's a product/design critique, not a code issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Gemfile:209 — new runtime gems ruby-readability and simple-rss expand the change into RSS ingestion and HTML scraping beyond the stated intent (P2)

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds embedding and feed-import functionality (EmbedController, PollFeed job, TopicEmbed.import_remote using ruby-readability, SimpleRSS usage) and even comments in the Gemfile that these gems are “required for feed importing and embedding.” The proposed finding claims this expands scope beyond “stated intent,” but no stated intent/requirements are present in the diff to verify a mismatch. Adding these runtime gems is consistent with the new code added and is not itself a bug, security issue, or clear defect evidenced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb:3 — whitespace-only churn plus removed trailing newline in an existing shipped migration (P3)

adjudication.rationale: The diff for db/migrate/20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb only changes whitespace (removes trailing spaces on a blank line) and results in the file lacking a final newline (shown by "\\ No newline at end of file"). These are formatting/style issues and do not introduce a functional bug, security issue, or correctness defect in the migration logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb:1 — `require_dependency 'email/sender'` is never used, a copy-paste leftover (P3)

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb`, the top-level `require_dependency 'email/sender'` is not referenced anywhere in the class/module. The job only looks up a `User` and calls `TopicRetriever.new(...).retrieve`. Nothing in this file uses `Email::Sender` (or constants from `email/sender`), so this is an unnecessary require (likely leftover) that adds avoidable loading/coupling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:20 — TOCTOU check-then-insert (`where(embed_url:).first` then `create!`) races between PollFeed and RetrieveTopic, raising RecordNotUnique that aborts the retry:false job (P1)

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.import`, it does `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and if blank it later does `TopicEmbed.create!(..., embed_url: url, ...)` (inside a transaction) while the migration adds a unique index on `topic_embeds.embed_url`. Two concurrent callers (e.g., `Jobs::PollFeed` iterating items and `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`/`TopicRetriever` fetching the same URL, or two PollFeed runs) can both observe no row and then both attempt `create!`, causing `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique`/`RecordNotUnique` from the DB. There is no rescue/retry handling here; `Jobs::PollFeed` explicitly sets `sidekiq_options retry: false`, so such an exception would fail the job and it won’t be retried, potentially skipping remaining feed items in that run.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:20,79 — embed_url is the identity key with zero normalization, so trailing slashes/utm params/id-vs-link fallbacks create duplicate topics for the same article (P1)

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The diff introduces `TopicEmbed` with `embed_url` as the unique identity (`add_index :topic_embeds, :embed_url, unique: true`) and all lookups are exact-string matches (`TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and `topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` does the same). There is no normalization/canonicalization of URLs (no stripping of trailing slashes, query params like `utm_*`, fragment removal, etc.). Callers also pass through potentially variant URLs (e.g., `PollFeed` uses `i.link` but falls back to `i.id` if link is blank/non-http), meaning the same article can be imported under different `embed_url` strings and will create separate topics instead of updating the existing one.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:46 — `open(url).read` has no open/read timeout and no size cap, letting one slow host block Sidekiq workers indefinitely with no circuit breaker (P1)

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import_remote the code fetches remote content via `open(url).read` (open-uri) with no explicit `open_timeout`/`read_timeout` options and no maximum download size enforcement. This runs in background retrieval paths (e.g., TopicRetriever/Jobs::RetrieveTopic), so a slow/unresponsive or very large response can tie up a Sidekiq worker for an extended time and/or consume excessive memory. The diff introduces this network call without any circuit-breaker/limits.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:41 — `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` runs a full feed fetch+import synchronously on a per-page-view cache miss, O(feed size) per miss (P1)
lib/topic_retriever.rb:26 — non-atomic `setnx` then `expire`; a crash between them leaves the key with no TTL, permanently blocking retrieval for that URL (P2)

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb `retrieved_recently?` does `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` followed by a separate `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. If the process crashes (or is killed) after `setnx` succeeds but before `expire` runs, the key will remain without a TTL. On subsequent calls `setnx` will return false, causing `retrieved_recently?` to return true forever for that `@embed_url`, permanently throttling retrieval for that URL. This is a real correctness issue introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:22 — `feed_key` is computed and never used; the implied If-Modified-Since conditional fetch was never implemented so the whole feed is reprocessed hourly (P2)

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb a `feed_key` method is defined (computes a SHA1-based key from `SiteSetting.feed_polling_url`) but it is never referenced anywhere in the file (nor in the shown diff). The `poll_feed` method always does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and then iterates `rss.items.each`, meaning every hourly run fetches/parses the full feed and attempts to import every item again. While `TopicEmbed.import` prevents duplicate embeds via `embed_url`/`content_sha1`, the job still reprocesses the whole feed each time and the unused `feed_key` indicates an unimplemented caching/conditional-fetch mechanism.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35 — no per-item rescue in `rss.items.each`, so one bad item drops every remaining item for that hour with retry: false (P2)

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed`, the code iterates `rss.items.each do |i|` and then calls methods on item fields without guards (e.g., `i.content.scrub`, `CGI.unescapeHTML(...)`, `TopicEmbed.import(...)`). If any single item is malformed (e.g., `i.content` is nil -> `NoMethodError` on `scrub`, or `TopicEmbed.import` raises), the exception will abort the entire job and skip the remaining items in that run. This is made worse by `sidekiq_options retry: false`, meaning the failed run will not be retried, so all remaining items are dropped until the next scheduled hour.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:4 — topic_id/post_id are null: false with no FK and no index, so orphan rows crash the next import with PostRevisor.new(nil) (P2)

adjudication.rationale: The migration creates `topic_embeds` with `topic_id`/`post_id` as `null: false` but without any foreign key constraints. In `TopicEmbed.import`, the update path does `post = embed.post` and then (when content changed) calls `PostRevisor.new(post)` without checking for `nil`. If a `topic_embeds` row becomes orphaned (e.g., its post/topic was deleted), `embed.post` will be `nil` and this will raise/crash on the next import/update attempt. The lack of FK enforcement makes such orphans possible, and there’s no defensive handling in the code shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 — in-place mutation of the contents argument means content_sha1 is computed over the footer-appended buffer, so a footer template change forces spurious re-revision of every embedded topic (P2)

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import, `contents << "...Imported from..."` does mutate the passed-in String and `content_sha1` is computed after that append, so the stored hash includes the injected footer. However, the footer is intentionally part of the post body being imported, and hashing the exact stored contents is a reasonable way to detect whether the *stored* post should be updated. Calling the resulting updates “spurious” if the footer text/template changes is a design judgment that isn’t verifiably a defect from the diff alone (it could be desired to propagate footer changes). The in-place mutation also doesn’t show a concrete bug in current call sites in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:20 — `discourse_expires_in 1.minute` is applied even on the `render 'loading'` branch, letting intermediaries cache the placeholder after the topic exists (P3)

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, the call to `discourse_expires_in 1.minute` is unconditionally executed after the `if topic_id ... else ... render 'loading'` branch. That means the response headers for the loading placeholder will also advertise a 1-minute cache lifetime. If a client/proxy caches that loading response, it can continue to serve the cached placeholder for up to a minute even after `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` starts returning a topic_id, delaying the real embed content.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb:3 — bare integer discriminator with no CHECK constraint; out-of-range cook_method values are representable and silently fall through (P3)

adjudication.rationale: The migration adds `posts.cook_method` as a plain `:integer` with `default: 1, null: false` and no DB-level constraint limiting values to the defined enum (`Post.cook_methods ||= Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)`). So technically out-of-range integers could be stored. However, in the code shown this does not create a clear defect: `Post#cook` explicitly treats only `:raw_html` specially and otherwise uses the normal cooking pipeline, meaning unexpected values simply behave like the default (regular) path rather than causing a verifiable bug/security issue. The absence of a CHECK constraint here is a general robustness suggestion, not a concrete problem demonstrated by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/post_revisor.rb:85 — `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])` globally lets any caller bypass Post validation, weakening validation in a task meant to enhance it (P1)

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `PostRevisor#update_post` from `@post.save` to `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])`, which does allow callers of `PostRevisor#revise!` to bypass ActiveRecord validations by passing `skip_validations: true`. However, in this diff that behavior is added to support the new embed/feed import path (`TopicEmbed.import` calls `revisor.revise!(..., skip_validations: true, ...)`), mirroring existing behavior in `PostCreator` where `skip_validations: true` was already used for imports. There’s no evidence in the diff that untrusted user-controlled input can set `skip_validations` on normal edit flows, so labeling this as a P1 “weakening validation” issue is not a clearly verifiable defect introduced by the change; it appears intentional and internally-scoped.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:11 — `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//` uses a line anchor not \A, so "javascript:alert(1)\nhttp://x" passes the one named URL-validation gate (P1)
app/models/post.rb:133 — a global raw-HTML rendering bypass of the sanitization pipeline is added to core Post as a side detail of an embed task (P1)

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The diff adds `Post.cook_methods` and changes `Post#cook` to `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, which bypasses the normal cooking/rendering pipeline (`post_analyzer.cook` + `Plugin::Filter.apply`). That pipeline is typically where sanitization/HTML safety would occur. The new `TopicEmbed.import` explicitly sets `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and imports HTML from RSS/readability (`SimpleRSS.parse ... i.content`, `Readability::Document.new(...).content`) without any sanitization step shown in the diff. As a result, imported content can be stored and then served as-is, creating a verifiable XSS/unsafe HTML injection risk and introducing a global bypass in core `Post` behavior for any post with that flag.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:44-49 — spec asserts synchronous TopicRetriever#retrieve while the controller now does Jobs.enqueue, so no green test witnesses the delivered behavior (P1)

adjudication.rationale: The finding is correct. In EmbedController#best, when no topic_id is found it now does `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, user_id: ..., embed_url: embed_url)` and renders 'loading'; it does not instantiate or call `TopicRetriever` directly. However, spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb (the example around the cited lines) stubs `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed` to nil and then expects `TopicRetriever.new` and `retriever.retrieve` to be called during the controller action. That expectation no longer matches the code in the diff and would fail, and it also doesn't assert the actual behavior (job enqueue).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:9-10 — embed_url is never validated at the entry point; validation was relocated to TopicRetriever#invalid_host? which runs only on the async path after the DB lookup (P2)

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best, `embed_url = params.require(:embed_url)` only enforces presence; there is no URL/host validation before using it to look up an existing `TopicEmbed` (`TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)`). Host/URI validation exists in `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?`, but that is only reached on the async path (when no embed is found and the job runs). If a `TopicEmbed` already exists for an `embed_url` whose host doesn’t match `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, the controller will still render that topic’s embed without any validation. Also, malformed `embed_url` values can cause the controller to enqueue work that will never run (retriever bails) and the iframe stays on the loading loop. This matches the finding’s claim that validation is missing at the entry point and only occurs later on the async path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:41 — a per-URL retrieval silently became a full-feed bulk import, an objective change not covered by the stated intent (P2)

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb, perform_retrieve is invoked for a single @embed_url, but when SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled? is true it unconditionally calls Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}). PollFeed#poll_feed parses the configured feed and iterates rss.items importing each item (TopicEmbed.import for every entry), i.e., a full-feed bulk import. This is objectively broader work than “retrieve a topic for an embedded URL” and can be triggered by a single per-URL retrieval path (even if later it returns early when the specific embed is found). This change is directly visible in the diff and can cause unintended extra imports/performance load.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:17 — origin check labeled as validation is a loose substring match that rejects nothing structurally (P2)
app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:11 — raw `request.referer` interpolated into a single-quoted JS string with no escape_javascript, giving reflected XSS via a referer containing a quote (P1)
matched_golden_ids: An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate issue flags that `request.referer` is interpolated raw into a JavaScript string in an ERB template without `escape_javascript`, enabling reflected XSS via malicious referer content. This is the same underlying vulnerability described in the golden comment (unescaped header leading to XSS).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 — the embed URL is interpolated unescaped into `<a href='#{url}'>` and stored with cook_method raw_html, giving unauthenticated stored XSS rendered by best.html.erb (P1)
app/models/topic_embed.rb:48-52 — Readability output keeps a[href]/img[src] from arbitrary remote HTML and is stored raw_html, so javascript:/data: hrefs bypass Discourse's sanitizer (P1)

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a `raw_html` cook method (Post#cook returns `raw` when `cook_method == :raw_html`) and uses it for imported content in `TopicEmbed.import` via `PostCreator.new(..., cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html])`. `TopicEmbed.import_remote` builds HTML from `ruby-readability` while allowing tags including `a`/`img` and attributes `href`/`src`, then stores `doc.content` without running Discourse’s normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. `absolutize_urls` only rewrites relative `/...` URLs and does not validate/strip `javascript:` or `data:` schemes. Finally, the embed view renders `raw post.cooked`, and for these posts `cooked == raw`. So attacker-controlled/compromised remote HTML containing `href="javascript:..."` or similar would be persisted and served unsanitized, which is a real XSS risk introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:14-19 — invalid_host? checks only host, never the scheme, and open-uri follows redirects, so ftp:// and 30x redirects to 127.0.0.1/169.254.169.254 give unauthenticated SSRF (P1)

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In lib/topic_retriever.rb, invalid_host? only compares URI(@embed_url).host to SiteSetting.embeddable_host and does not restrict the scheme/protocol. That means an embed_url like ftp://<embeddable_host>/... passes validation (URI host matches) and later fetch_http calls TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, @embed_url), which does open(url).read (TopicEmbed#import_remote). open-uri will fetch non-HTTP schemes it supports and, for HTTP(S), will follow redirects by default; since the code does not re-validate the final redirected location, an attacker-controlled URL on the allowed host can 30x redirect to internal/metadata IPs (e.g., 127.0.0.1 or 169.254.169.254), resulting in SSRF. The referer-based check in EmbedController can be spoofed by a direct HTTP client, so this is plausibly unauthenticated.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:30 — `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` passes an unvalidated setting to Kernel#open, so a leading '|' is command execution and file:/// reads local files (P2)
matched_golden_ids: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point to the same root problem: PollFeed passes the unvalidated SiteSetting.feed_polling_url into Kernel#open, allowing attacker-controlled URL fetching. The candidate additionally notes other Kernel#open dangers (pipe command execution, file:// reads), but it still covers the golden SSRF issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26 — referer host equality is the only framing authorization and is paired with X-Frame-Options ALLOWALL, and the per-URL throttle lets an anon attacker drive unbounded outbound fetches (P2)
matched_golden_ids: The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same core security issue: X-Frame-Options set to ALLOWALL (disabling clickjacking protection) and framing authorization relying solely on Referer host checking (which is weak/spoofable). It doesn’t mention the nil/empty-string fallback detail, but it captures the main problem described in the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:17 — substring origin test plus no `e.source === iframe.contentWindow` check lets a foreign frame control iframe height (P3)
spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:35 — `poller.expects(:poll_feed).once` mocks out the unit under test, leaving the entire new poll_feed body untested (P1)

adjudication.rationale: In spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb the example at ~line 35 is explicitly testing Jobs::PollFeed#execute’s guard conditions and that it delegates to #poll_feed when settings are present. Stubbing/expecting poll_feed there does not “mock out the unit under test”; the unit under test in that example is execute, not the poll_feed implementation. While it’s true there is no direct test of the poll_feed method body in this diff, lack of coverage is not a verifiable defect introduced by the code, and the spec’s delegation expectation is a valid pattern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb:11,33,39 — `expects(:perform_retrieve)` stubs the method under test, so the existing-embed short-circuit, inline PollFeed call, and fetch_http are all uncovered (P1)

adjudication.rationale: In `spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb`, the expectations are placed on the private helper `perform_retrieve` while the actual method under test is `TopicRetriever#retrieve`. Using `expects(:perform_retrieve)` here is intentional to assert whether `retrieve` delegates (or not) based on host/throttle conditions; it does not “stub the method under test.” While it’s true these specs don’t exercise `perform_retrieve` internals (existing-embed short-circuit, PollFeed, `fetch_http`), that’s a test coverage concern rather than a verifiable defect introduced by this diff, and the finding mischaracterizes what is being tested.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:18-28 — guard specs never stub feed_polling_enabled? (default false), so they pass even if the feed_polling_url/embed_by_username clauses were deleted (P1)

adjudication.rationale: In Jobs::PollFeed#execute, the first guard is `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?`. In spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb the “requires feed_polling_url” and “requires embed_by_username” examples only stub feed_polling_url/embed_by_username to nil, but do not stub `feed_polling_enabled?` to true. Given the default in config/site_settings.yml is `feed_polling_enabled: false`, `execute` will short-circuit on the first condition and never reach the feed_polling_url/embed_by_username checks. Therefore those specs would still pass even if the latter clauses were removed, so the finding correctly identifies a real weakness/defect in the tests added by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:48 — `TopicView.expects(:new)` returns nil and the after-hook `response.should be_success` is vacuous with view rendering disabled (P1)

adjudication.rationale: In `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb`, the example "creates a topic view when a topic_id is found" sets `TopicView.expects(:new).with(123, nil, {best: 5})` without specifying a return value, so Mocha will indeed return `nil`. However, in an RSpec controller spec, view rendering is typically stubbed/disabled by default unless `render_views` is enabled, so the template code that would dereference `@topic_view` is not executed here. As a result, the spec is intentionally only asserting that `TopicView.new` is called; it is not required to return a real `TopicView` instance for this test to be valid. The `response.should be_success` assertion is still meaningful for the controller action execution path. Therefore this is not a clear, verifiable defect introduced by the diff; it’s more a critique of test completeness/style rather than a real problem.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/embed/best.html.erb:6 — no spec uses render_views, so the entire new view layer including the invalid `<%- end if %>` is untested (P1)

adjudication.rationale: The new template `app/views/embed/best.html.erb` contains `<%- end if %>`, which is invalid Ruby/ERB syntax (you can’t apply an `if` modifier to `end`), so rendering the view would raise a syntax error. The added controller spec (`spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb`) does not enable `render_views`, so it would not exercise/compile this template and therefore would not catch the error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:8-11 — "is 404 without an embed_url" passes for the wrong reason (blank embeddable_host raises first); params.require has zero coverage (P2)

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController`, `before_filter :ensure_embeddable` runs before `best`, and it raises if `SiteSetting.embeddable_host.blank?`. In the spec "is 404 without an embed_url" (`get :best` with no stubs), `embeddable_host` defaults to '' per `site_settings.yml`, so the request fails due to `ensure_embeddable` ("embeddable host not set") before reaching `params.require(:embed_url)`. Thus the example can pass without actually exercising the missing-`embed_url` path, and there is no spec that sets a valid `embeddable_host`/referer while omitting `embed_url` to cover `params.require`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb:34,40 — stubbing retrieved_recently? replaces the real redis throttle, leaving setnx/expire and the staff no_throttle bypass unexercised (P2)

adjudication.rationale: The cited lines in `spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb` intentionally stub `retrieved_recently?` to control the branch outcome when testing `TopicRetriever#retrieve` calling (or not calling) `perform_retrieve`. This does mean the Redis throttle implementation (`$redis.setnx`/`expire`) and the `no_throttle` bypass are not exercised by these particular examples, but that is a test-coverage concern, not a verifiable bug/correctness/security defect introduced by the diff. The production code still uses Redis throttling unless explicitly bypassed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:42-44 — `TopicRetriever.expects(:new)` has no .with constraint, so embed_url/user_id/no_throttle propagation is unverified (P2)

adjudication.rationale: In spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb the expectation `TopicRetriever.expects(:new).returns(retriever)` indeed lacks a `.with(...)` argument constraint, but that is only a test-strength/coverage nit rather than a verifiable bug/security/correctness defect introduced by this diff. Also, the diff’s EmbedController#best does not call `TopicRetriever.new` at all—it enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, user_id: ..., embed_url: ...)`—so the finding’s claim about verifying propagation of `embed_url/user_id/no_throttle` through `TopicRetriever.new` is not grounded in the actual code path shown here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb:39-42 — the update spec asserts only cooked content, never that no duplicate topic was created nor that content_sha1 advanced (P2)

adjudication.rationale: The cited lines in `spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb` do only assert that `post.cooked` contains the new contents after a second `TopicEmbed.import` call, and they do not assert that no new `Topic`/`TopicEmbed` was created or that `content_sha1` changed. However, this is a test-coverage/completeness observation, not a verifiable defect introduced by the diff in application code. The production logic in `TopicEmbed.import` clearly reuses an existing `TopicEmbed` by `embed_url` and updates `content_sha1` via `update_column` when it changes. The finding does not identify a real bug/security/correctness issue in the diff itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:41 — import_remote, topic_id_for_embed, and absolutize_urls' non-default-port branch have zero test coverage in this diff (P2)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add methods that are not directly exercised by the new specs: `TopicEmbed.import_remote` isn’t tested, `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed` is only stubbed in the controller spec (so its implementation isn’t executed), and the `absolutize_urls` non-default-port branch isn’t hit by the provided tests (they use an `http://...` URL without an explicit non-80/443 port). However, “zero test coverage” is a quality/process concern rather than a concrete bug/security/correctness defect introduced by the code itself, so it doesn’t qualify as a real, verifiable problem in the diff under the given criteria.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb:36 — asserts only row existence, never the embed_url/content_sha1/post_id values the new code writes (P3)

adjudication.rationale: The cited line in spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb does only check that a TopicEmbed row exists for the topic ("TopicEmbed.where(topic_id: post.topic_id).should be_present") and does not assert embed_url/content_sha1/post_id values. However, this is a test-coverage completeness suggestion, not a verifiable defect/bug/security/correctness issue introduced by the diff. The code does set those fields (TopicEmbed.create! with embed_url/content_sha1/post_id), and nothing in the diff indicates they are wrong or untestable. So the finding does not identify a real problem in the change, only a potential improvement to the spec.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3 — `force: true` added to an already-shipped migration drops the existing top_topics table and all rows on any re-run, with no rollback path (P0)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add `force: true` to `create_table :top_topics`, which would drop/recreate the table *if that migration were executed while the table already exists*. However, Rails migrations are not re-run once applied (tracked in `schema_migrations`), so this does not cause data loss on a normal `db:migrate`. Also, the migration uses `def change` with `create_table`, which is reversible (rollback drops the table), so the claim of “no rollback path” is incorrect. The finding overstates the impact and is not a clearly verifiable defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:3 — `force: true` arms a destructive re-run of topic_embeds, whose loss turns every future import into a duplicate topic (P1)

adjudication.rationale: The new migration `CreateTopicEmbeds` uses `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true`, which instructs Rails to drop the table if it already exists before recreating it. That is a destructive operation on reruns (e.g., db:migrate:redo, accidental re-application, or running on a DB where the table pre-exists), and would wipe `topic_embeds` rows. Since `TopicEmbed.import` relies on that table to detect existing `embed_url` mappings, losing it would make subsequent imports treat existing URLs as new and create duplicate topics/posts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:35-37 — content_sha1 is updated unconditionally even when revise! returns false, so the new upstream content is silently lost forever (P1)

db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb:3 — add_column with default+null:false rewrites posts under an exclusive lock, and code reading cook_method can deploy before the migration lands (P2)

adjudication.rationale: The migration `20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb` adds `cook_method` to the large `posts` table with both `default: 1` and `null: false`. On PostgreSQL versions prior to 11, this pattern rewrites the whole table and can take an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock for the duration, impacting availability. Separately, the diff introduces runtime reads/writes of `posts.cook_method` (e.g., `Post#cook`, `PostCreator#setup_post`), so deploying the code before the migration would raise errors due to the missing column in any process hitting those paths. Both issues are directly implied by the diff changes (migration + new code usage).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:20-28 — no FK or dependent handling to posts/topics; one orphan row aborts the entire feed import loop (P2)

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new TopicEmbed model/table with `belongs_to :topic` and `belongs_to :post`, but the migration (`create_topic_embeds`) only adds integer columns and an index—no foreign key constraints—and the model does not specify any dependent cleanup on `Topic`/`Post` deletion. That makes orphan `topic_embeds` rows possible (e.g., if a post/topic is deleted elsewhere). In `TopicEmbed.import`, the update path does `post = embed.post` and, if the content hash changed, immediately calls `PostRevisor.new(post)` without guarding against `post` being nil. If an orphan exists, this will raise and would abort the RSS import loop in `Jobs::PollFeed` (exceptions inside `rss.items.each` stop the job).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:31-37 — an embed_url longer than varchar(255) raises inside an unrescued loop on a retry:false job, skipping every remaining item (P2)

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` the code iterates `rss.items.each` and calls `TopicEmbed.import(user, url, ...)` (lines ~31-37). `TopicEmbed` is created with `embed_url` as a `string` with no explicit limit in the migration (`CreateTopicEmbeds`), which in Rails defaults to VARCHAR(255). If a feed item’s `link`/`id` is longer than 255, `TopicEmbed.create!` will raise a DB error (e.g., value too long / string truncation). There is no rescue in the loop, so the exception aborts the job and the remaining feed items in that run are skipped. The job explicitly sets `sidekiq_options retry: false`, so Sidekiq will not retry the failed execution automatically.
